title: My balancing loop for an AI-built roguelite: players' real builds, a test bench, and a bot at 20x speed
author: Groowl
selftext:
Balancing a roguelite with 63 stacking upgrades by feel is impossible: the combinations grow faster than your playtime. So with Claude Code I built a loop that does most of it for me.

1. Collect what players really do. The online leaderboard doesn't only store times: every run sends its final build and the order the upgrades were picked. A private export page lets me see which builds dominate, and in what order people take them.

2. Turn that into test cases. The builds that keep showing up go into a list: which upgrades, in which order, which ones scale over the run.

3. Let a bot play them. The game is a single HTML file, so a Node script loads it into a sandbox with a fake browser and runs the real game code headless, about 20x faster than real time, one run per CPU core. The bot aims, buys stats, picks the upgrades of the build, and reports how far it gets in endless mode.

4. Read the table, change one number. Claude edits the upgrade's math (each upgrade has its own function), and every change goes into the patch notes as before → after.

5. Rerun the bench. If the build still towers over everything else, again.

A real example: WHETSTONE combined with BOOMERANG and BLOODLUST was sitting at the top of the endless table, so its scaling went from +30% to +26% at max level. And a surprise the bench showed me: a build with no scaling upgrade at all reaches room 65, as far as the BLOODLUST builds. I'd never have guessed that by playing.

What Claude still can't do: tell me if the result is fun. That part is mine.

How do you test balance in your AI-assisted games? Does anyone else let the AI run the numbers?

The game: https://groowl.itch.io/shuriken-slam-jam-demo
